sections.html:
Manchester is a Hartford County town about 10 miles east of Hartford's Union Station. The 2020 census counted 59,713 residents over 27.7 square miles, and ZIP codes run from 06040 to 06042 plus 06045. One town government assesses, bills and collects for every neighborhood.

The silk and woolen mills that earned the nickname Silk City left a lot of older housing behind. Homes built for mill workers and the streets that grew around them are now a century or more old, so wiring, plumbing and roofs are what buyers look at first. Three interstates (I-84, I-384 and I-291) and several Connecticut Transit bus routes link the town to Hartford. No passenger rail stops here; the nearest station is Union Station.

Because the town runs one assessment office and one collector for every neighborhood, the same two offices answer your questions whether the house is near the old mill district or out toward the edge of town.

Manchester is revaluing every property for an October 1, 2026 assessment date. State law puts towns on a five-year cycle, and the Assessment Office's revaluation overview walks through each step. The town hired Tyler Technologies to do the work.

Data collection and market analysis started in early 2026 and ran into September, with mailers to residential owners and visits to some parcels, especially recent purchases and homes with permitted work. Valuation followed. Notices of the new values were scheduled for fall 2026, and informal meetings with assessment staff come after the notices.

If you may sell, read your notice carefully. The informal meeting is the place to fix wrong details on your property record, such as room counts or square footage, before they feed the next tax bill.

Real estate tax comes in two installments, July 1 and January 1. Both payment coupons arrive together in the June mailing, and no second bill follows for January, so keep the first one safe. A missing bill does not cancel the tax or the interest.

Tax not paid on or before August 1 is delinquent. Interest then runs at 1.5% per month back to the original due date, and the minimum charge on any delinquent tax is $2.00. To stay clear of interest, a payment must be postmarked by August 1.

  • Pay online, by phone at 1-844-562-1959, by mail, or in the drop box behind Town Hall. The box does not take cash.
  • Call the Collector of Revenue at 860-647-3018 or write to collector@manchesterct.gov.
DayCollector of Revenue hours at Town Hall

Those hours come from the town's tax payment notice, so call before you drive over.

sections.h2: Checking your property record before you list
sections.html:
The revaluation turns your property record into the basis for the next tax bill, and a buyer will see that record too. Pull it before you list and read it line by line. The details that go wrong most often are finished square footage, the count of bathrooms and bedrooms, and whether an addition or a finished basement is described correctly. If a data collector visited your parcel, ask what they recorded. Recent purchases and homes with permitted work were the ones visited most, so an owner who pulled a permit in the last few years has a particular reason to check.

Bring photos or the permit paperwork to the informal meeting. Staff can compare what you show them with what the record says, and an error corrected now will not follow the house into the buyer's first bill.

sections.h2: What the revaluation does not change
sections.html:
A new value is not a new bill by itself. The assessment is only one half of the tax calculation, and the rest depends on the mill rate the town sets. Do not assume your tax will rise or fall in step with the new number. Instead, wait for the notice, compare it with recent sales of similar houses nearby, and use the informal meeting if something looks off.

Selling during the transition is still possible. A buyer will ask what the new assessment is, so have the notice in your folder next to the tax bill. If a notice has not reached you, contact the Assessment Office rather than guessing.

sections.h2: Selling a Manchester house with tax due
sections.html:
You do not need cash on hand. The title company or closing attorney asks the Collector of Revenue for a payoff and settles the amount from your proceeds at closing. The usual order of work is short.

  1. Ask the Collector of Revenue for the balance and the status of each installment.
  2. Give that figure to your closing attorney.
  3. Confirm whether the next bill will go to you or to the buyer after the deed changes hands.
  4. Set the closing date once the payoff is in writing.

Bring the latest bill and a photo ID. Estates should also bring the papers that show who may sign. If tenants live in the house, tell them early that a title company may be in touch, and plan around any lease that runs past your closing.

Delinquent tax does not freeze the process, but interest keeps running back to the original due date, so the sooner the payoff is requested the smaller the surprise. Ask for a figure good through your expected closing date, and ask again if that date moves.

The state conveyance tax return, Form OP-236, is filed when the deed is recorded, and Manchester's town code on it is 077. The Department of Revenue Services lists the exemptions. Two matter here: a principal residence conveyed in lieu of foreclosure, and a principal residence with a pyrrhotite-damaged foundation, which requires a professional engineer's written evaluation.

Manchester's Assessment Office also keeps a page on defective concrete and crumbling foundations. If you suspect a foundation problem, start with that page and an engineer, because it changes both what the house can sell for and how it can be sold.

Older houses are the common thread. A house with outdated systems, a tenant in place or taxes behind can be hard to list on the open market. Some owners are also trying to decide whether to sell before or after the revaluation notices land, and that is worth a call to the Assessment Office.

A cash sale is a fair option to compare against listing, particularly when the repair bill is large. Cash Home Buyers purchases Manchester houses as-is, with repairs, back taxes or tenants in place. You skip repairs and showings, and the title company pays what is owed from the proceeds.

faqs.q: When are Manchester real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: July 1 and January 1. A payment postmarked by August 1 counts as on time for the July installment.

faqs.q: What interest rate does Manchester charge?
faqs.a: Interest is 1.5% per month, counted back to the original due date. Any delinquent tax carries a minimum charge of $2.00.
Yes. The 2026 revaluation uses an October 1, 2026 assessment date. New-value notices were scheduled for fall 2026, with informal meetings afterward.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Manchester house if taxes are unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax is settled from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the Collector of Revenue for the current payoff in writing, with interest figured to your closing date.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Manchester tax collector?
faqs.a: Call 860-647-3018 or email collector@manchesterct.gov. Check the town website for current office hours, which have varied by weekday.
